source.title: Discovering Millions of Interpretable Features with Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Xinyang He; Wei Wang; Bing Zhao; Xuan-Cheng Ren; Wen-Bo Li; Wei Qiao; Hu Wei; Lin Qu

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or document mismatch; the paper text includes its conclusion and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Uses the difference-in-means refusal direction to select a layer and an SAE feature, then reports refusal rates for steering with the SAE decoder feature. It does not report outcomes for adding or ablating the difference-in-means direction itself.
record.gate_note: Appendix D describes candidate-direction ablation, addition, and KL metrics used to select a direction, but reports no results for those metrics; these selection-only evaluations are not rows. The reported intervention instead steers with a selected SAE decoder feature.
record.test_reason: The paper uses Arditi et al.'s difference-in-means method (bypass, induce and KL scores) only to pick a layer (Appendix D). It reports no ablation or addition results for that direction. All reported refusal outcomes come from adding an SAE decoder feature (Table 2, Fig. 10), a related but different intervention. The direction itself serves only as a selection tool.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that selected SAE features causally steer Qwen3-1.7B/4B-instruct toward refusal, reaching the highest unsafe-prompt refusal of the three methods. They note that gains are weaker on WildGuard and that refusal on safe prompts also rises with alpha. They also find an inverted-U in unsafe refusal versus alpha, and that the larger model responds more strongly.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses difference-in-means to identify a candidate layer/direction, then selects and adds an SAE decoder feature at that layer; it does not report a direct intervention result for the original difference-in-means vector.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported feature-steering refusal rates vary by dataset and prompt class. Appendix E states that unsafe refusal rates peak around α ≈ 0.3–0.5 and fall near zero at larger coefficients; safe-prompt refusal rises with α. These are SAE-feature steering results, not direct tests of the claim's direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding a single selected SAE decoder feature at layer 18/19 raises unsafe-prompt refusal in Qwen3-1.7B (e.g. Mix 0.417→0.667) and Qwen3-4B (XSTest 0.685→0.95). Safe-prompt refusal also rises (4B XSTest 0.032→0.516). Random-feature steering drives refusal near zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single SAE feature, found at a layer chosen by difference-in-means selection, can induce refusal in instruction-tuned Qwen3 models, at the cost of over-refusal on safe prompts.

record.code_released: not stated; the text says code and model weights will be released in the coming months.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the refusal-rate table. The experiment is a single refusal-steering case study and does not report a direct result for ablation or addition of the selected difference-in-means direction. General capability preservation is not tested; the KL criterion is described for direction selection but its outcomes are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted. Appendix D's candidate-direction ablation, addition, and KL values are described as selection criteria but are not reported as outcomes.

untested.parts: No reported ablation or addition outcome for the difference-in-means direction. No capability-preservation results; the KL score was used only as a selection filter.
No jailbreak analysis or adversarial training.
No multi-direction, cone or affine analysis.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal.
No reasoning-model test; Qwen3 is used in instruct mode.

record.verdict_notes: The main contribution is the release of an SAE suite; refusal steering is a small case study. The random-feature control collapsing refusal to about 0, rather than leaving it at baseline, suggests the steering magnitude is disruptive in itself, which weakens the comparison. Baseline rows r01–r12 duplicate the baselines already carried in the steering rows; r07–r12 are mislabeled as 1.7B when they belong to 4B. No uncertainty estimates are given. The refusal metric is substring matching.

versions.untested_parts: No reported outcome for ablation or addition of the difference-in-means direction itself, or for preservation of other abilities.
No attack suppression experiment or training against ablation.
No test of whether refusal is affine, conical, or carried by multiple directions.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or other transfer test of the direction.
No comparison of refusal training methods or stages.
